title: Maximum induced emf
description: Essential: The student must correctly calculate the peak induced electromotive force (Em = NBSω).

title: Effective voltage and current
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the effective voltage (U_eff = Em/√2) and the ammeter reading (I_eff = U_eff / R).

title: Resistor thermal power
description: Important: The student must apply Joule's law (P = I_eff² R) to find the power dissipated in the resistor.

title: External work calculation
description: Important: The student must relate the work done by the external force to the total electrical energy dissipated (W = P_total * t).

title: Angular velocity from speed
description: Important: The student must correctly convert the rotational speed (120 rpm) to angular velocity (ω).

title: Neon bulb flashing frequency
description: Important: The student must recognize the neon bulb flashes twice per AC cycle and calculate the flashing frequency (2 * f_AC).

title: Voltage threshold timing
description: Important: For part (5), the student must find the angular intervals where the instantaneous voltage exceeds the bulb's firing voltage.

title: Total illumination time
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the total time the bulb is lit over 10 minutes, based on the fraction of each cycle it is on.

title: Peak vs. effective value confusion
description: Pitfall: Using the peak voltage (Em) instead of the effective value (U_eff) in RMS current or power calculations.

title: Unit conversion error
description: Pitfall: Failing to convert coil dimensions from cm to m, or rotational speed from rpm to rad/s correctly.
